advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile det_measurement_provenance.py's docstring (lines 14-16) with the parser: either collapse the docstring example to the pinned single-line form, or make the parser accept a wrapped continuation.
evidence: Docstring shows a wrapped form: det_measurement_provenance.py:14-16 `    - [ ] [operator-attested] <criterion text>` / `          provenance: environment=<v>; ...; instrument=<v>` / `          — <justification>`

`_find_provenance_line` returns a single line only (det_measurement_provenance.py:100-101 `if _PROVENANCE_LINE_RE.match(stripped):` / `return stripped`) and never accumulates following continuation lines

`_parse_provenance` splits the justification off that single line's text: det_measurement_provenance.py:108-109 `if "—" in rest:` / `body, justification = rest.split("—", 1)`; a wrapped `—` line is never seen, so `justification=""` → flagged at 162-163

The canonical form pinned elsewhere is SINGLE-line: prompt `plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md:26` and ADR `0061-...md:58` both put `... instrument=<...> — <justification>` on one line, and ticket f161 §1a says 'in one canonical single-line form' — so the docstring's wrapped example is the inconsistent artifact
ABSENCE: no test in test_det_measurement_provenance.py or test_det_measurement_provenance_heldout.py exercises a multi-physical-line declaration; all use single-line `_GOOD`/`_decl`
advisory.finding: The module docstring documents a MULTI-LINE provenance declaration (the `— <justification>` on a separate continuation line), but the parser only reads the single physical line beginning with `provenance:` and splits the justification within that same line. A declaration wrapped as the docstring illustrates would be wrongly flagged as having a missing justification (and any wrapped key/value pairs as missing keys).
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the module docstring's example to the single-line canonical form used in the ADR/prompt/ticket, or extend _find_provenance_line to gather subsequent more-indented non-key lines into the provenance text before parsing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the origin/main-dependent tests skip (or resolve a merge-base fallback) when the ref is absent instead of failing/erroring.
evidence: test_measurement_provenance_criterion.py:129-135 `subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "--exit-code", "origin/main", "--", path], ...)` — a missing origin/main makes git exit non-zero, failing with the misleading message 'was modified — that changes the contract for ALL clients'

test_measurement_provenance_criterion.py:143-149 `subprocess.run(["git", "show", f"origin/main:{GENERATED_GUIDE}"], ..., check=True)` — `check=True` raises CalledProcessError (an error, not a clean assertion) when origin/main is unavailable
advisory.finding: Two overlay-wiring tests depend on the `origin/main` git ref being present and fetched (`git diff origin/main` and `git show origin/main:<path>` with check=True). In a shallow CI clone, a worktree without the `origin` remote, or a detached fixture checkout, these will error rather than assert the intended property.
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard with a `pytest.importorskip`-style check: run `git rev-parse --verify origin/main` first and `pytest.skip(...)` if it is missing, so the assertion only runs where the ref exists.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-substring grep in test_det_check_has_no_world_measurement_reach with a behavioral assertion (e.g. run provenance_gaps under a monkeypatched socket/subprocess that raises on any call, or assert the module imports resolve to stdlib-only) so the 'no network/shell reach' contract is verified by behavior, not by grepping the implementation text.
evidence: for forbidden in ("boto3", "botocore", "subprocess", "requests", "urllib", "socket", "httpx"): assert forbidden not in src

This is source-grepping: the assertion is over the text of the module under test, not any observable behavior; an `import socket as s`, an indirect reach via a helper module, or `os.system(...)` would leave the substring absent yet violate the 'pure text check, no network/shell' contract — and the check would false-positive if any token appears in a comment/docstring.
advisory.finding: test_det_check_has_no_world_measurement_reach asserts the 'no network/shell reach' contract by grepping the SOURCE UNDER TEST for module-name substrings, which tests the implementation text rather than its behavior and can be evaded (aliased import `import socket as s`, indirect import through another module, or `os.system`) while the contract is still violated.
scenarios: A future edit introduces a network call via an aliased or indirect import; the grep stays green while the behavioral contract is broken.
A docstring mentions one of the forbidden tokens and the test fails despite no behavior change.
advisory.suggested_fix: Exercise provenance_gaps/provenance_issues with socket.socket, subprocess.Popen and urllib.request.urlopen monkeypatched to raise, asserting no exception is raised — this verifies the runtime property rather than the source text.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add a test pinning that a multi-line (wrapped-justification) provenance declaration is handled, or correct the module/test docstrings to show only the single-line canonical form pinned by ticket §1a so the documented shape matches what the code and tests actually accept.
evidence: Module docstring depicts multi-line form: `provenance: environment=<v>; ... instrument=<v>` then a separate line `      — <justification>` (det_measurement_provenance.py:14-16).

_find_provenance_line returns a single `stripped` line (det_measurement_provenance.py:100-102); _parse_provenance only receives that one line and splits its own text on the em-dash (lines 105-119) — it never consumes a following wrapped line.

All fixtures (_GOOD in test_det_measurement_provenance.py:23-28, _decl in test_det_measurement_provenance_heldout.py:31-39) place the entire declaration on one physical line, so the wrapped form the docstrings advertise is never asserted.

Ticket §1a pins the canonical form as single-line, so this is a docstring/example-vs-code inconsistency rather than a contract-scope gap — but the in-repo docstrings assert a shape the code would mishandle and no test pins.
advisory.finding: The canonical declaration form documented in det_measurement_provenance.py (lines 14-16) and in the happy-path test docstring (lines 6-8) shows the em-dash justification WRAPPED onto a second continuation line, but no test exercises a multi-line provenance declaration; _find_provenance_line returns only the single `provenance:` line and _parse_provenance never joins the following line, so a wrapped justification would be treated as absent and falsely flagged. Every fixture keeps the whole declaration on one line, leaving this documented shape untested.
scenarios: An author copies the wrapped example from the module docstring; the lint reports the justification as missing on an otherwise-complete declaration.
